editorialThesis: A local practice travels through recordings, images and people; new communities make it speak their own lives. The reader moves from selected global milestones to a close reading of eight South Asian scenes.
mapNote: Selected cultural connections, not a complete map of origins.

chapters.headline: A neighbourhood makes a sound.
chapters.body: On 11 August 1973, Cindy Campbell and DJ Kool Herc threw a party at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue. It became a landmark in hip-hop’s beginnings. Around the Bronx, DJs, MCs, dancers and writers built a culture from the material at hand: records, walls, words and a crowd.

chapters.headline: The party leaves the block.
chapters.body: The Sugarhill Gang put “Rapper’s Delight” on record in 1979. The next wave travelled through screens: Wild Style reached Tokyo with its performers in 1983; Sidney brought H.I.P. H.O.P. to French television in 1984. Records and moving images gave distant audiences a way into the culture.

chapters.headline: Every city changes the sound.
chapters.body: MC Solaar released his French-language debut in 1991. In Heidelberg, Advanced Chemistry confronted racism on “Fremd im eigenen Land” in 1992. That year, Seo Taiji and Boys brought rap into Korean pop. In east London, pirate radio carried emerging grime voices. Local language, politics and musical traditions shaped what came next.

chapters.headline: The stories get closer to home.
chapters.body: Bohemia’s Punjabi rap grew out of life in California. Young Stunners uploaded “Burger-E-Karachi” in 2013. In Bombay, DIVINE and Naezy’s “Mere Gully Mein” put neighbourhood life into a 2015 release. By 2019, Nas’s Mass Appeal and Universal had launched a Mumbai label with DIVINE. South Asian stories were finding new routes between local listeners and the world.

chapters.headline: Eight scenes. Many ways to listen.
chapters.body: Bombay, Punjabi, Delhi, Urdu, Pune, Goa, Amd and Koshur. Explore selected releases from 29 artists, scene by scene. Each ring follows an artist; each coloured band marks a release. Choose a band to meet the project, or compare the same dates in the release list.

milestones.label: The Bronx
milestones.event: Cindy Campbell and Kool Herc’s Sedgwick Avenue party
milestones.qualification: A commemorated landmark, not a claim that one party instantly created all hip-hop practices.

milestones.label: London
milestones.event: Beat This! brings hip-hop to British television audiences
milestones.qualification: Selected media milestone; UK scenes and sound-system influences have wider histories.

milestones.label: Paris
milestones.event: Sidney presents H.I.P. H.O.P. on TF1
milestones.qualification: INA’s catalogue dates its first transmission14January1984. Useyearonlyifavoidingdisputedpopular14/15Januaryaccounts.

milestones.label: Tokyo
milestones.event: Wild Style release and cast tour
milestones.qualification: Explicit NewYork-to-Tokyo performer tour. Not a claim that no hip-hop records previously circulated in Japan.

milestones.label: Heidelberg
milestones.event: Advanced Chemistry release Fremd im eigenen Land
milestones.qualification: Use Heidelberg, not Berlin, for this group’s specific milestone.

milestones.label: Seoul
milestones.event: Seo Taiji and Boys’ rap-influenced pop debut
milestones.qualification: Seoul represents the national music industry;1992 is a mainstream breakthrough, not hip-hop’s first arrival in Korea.

milestones.label: California
milestones.event: Bohemia combines Punjabi poetry with Californian rap influences
milestones.qualification: Bay Area point is representative; source is a direct2009 interview hosted in an archive, supplemented by UrbanAsian2014 originalinterview. Avoid a precise first-release date as current Appleeditionis2004andoriginalreported2002.

milestones.label: Punjab
milestones.event: Punjabi rap connects listeners across Punjab and the diaspora
milestones.qualification: Representative regional hub, not a one-country boundary or birthplacerestriction.

milestones.label: Bombay
milestones.event: DIVINE and Naezy release Mere Gully Mein
milestones.qualification: 2015 is this release date, not the start of rap in India.

milestones.label: Karachi
milestones.qualification: Artist upload year, not a claim that Urdu rap began in this year. Karachi is a representative hub. Do not render an inevitable Punjab-to-Bombay-to-Karachi chain.

doNotCarryOver: No claim that hip-hop is globally the biggest or dominant genre; original chart lacks usable provenance.
Do not label commercial artists inauthentic or oppose them to an authentic underground.
No colonizing one-way tree in which each country copies its predecessor; use selected connections plus independent local nodes.
No precise South Asian origin date inferred from a streaming catalog reissue; display broad eras where evidence only supports eras.
No India-only descriptor for Urdu or Punjabi diaspora scenes; use South Asia and its diaspora.
No figure purporting to count all hip-hop scenes or releases;111 is the curated collection’s unique projectcount.
